::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Jan 12th [1864]  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS Society of Antiquaries 444/17/144
:::

My dear [Florence](people/person_1520.qmd),

Many thanks to you and your friend for your kindness about the pantomime. I am sorry however to say that I do not think it will quite do. I suppose it is the sort of thing to be done not so much by a regular narrative of the scenes as by some clever sketch such as perhaps takes an older hand. I hope it will not be a disappointment, but I think from your letter you have prepared her for it. I am glad you like some of the [Events of the Month](organizations/other_69.qmd), I think it will improve by practice. You have not told me the fate of Christina with the [Churchman](organizations/other_62.qmd), I greatly think that serial is improving under the new <u>[Master](people/person_1328.qmd)</u> - there is a very good story beginning.[^1] I am so glad your foot is better - I have some friends staying here and not much time so I must finish

yours sincerely
C Yonge

---

[^1]: Black-edged paper.
[^2]: Felicia Skene had recently taken over as editor of the *Churchman's Companion*.  A story called 'Christina' appears in Wilford's *A Vantage Ground and Other Stories* Reprinted from the *Monthly Packet* and the *Churchman's Companion* (London: Masters 1879).
